notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that no notification goes to Diana Johnson's personal address (diana.johnson.15@personal.example.com, on her HR profile); one pass has it, the other does not; kept because the request names her official address and the personal one is the near match a loose reading of 'her email address' would pick, the boundary of the recipient, with a lookup by personal email among the tools.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (all seven checks kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The request calls the case both a 'checking case' and one under the 'designated other account'; checking and other are both stored account types, so the two words conflict. The benchmark tests 'other', the word attached to the account itself, and that is kept; checking is not tested.
The case's short description 'Deployment: Diana Johnson' is 25 characters, below the policy's 30-character minimum, and does not follow its 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' template; the request names it exactly and the benchmark tests it exactly, so it is kept, though a policy-strict agent could halt here instead of creating the case and its notification.
The acting user (Tommy Jacobs) is an administrator; the policy lets administrators create services and change users, groups and roles, but bars them from routine HR case work. The case is part of the set-up the request asks for, so it is required.
The policy's role names (hr_manager and so on) do not match the stored role names; 'manager' is the stored value. Diana Johnson's user_role row (role 3, agent) is not tested: no listed tool names it and the benchmark tests only user.role.
coe_type, opened_by, assignment and the service's template and criteria are not stated and not tested. The other HR Service Desk member (user 22) is outside the removal's selector: the request clears only her association.
